Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

HDXBoxeR 0.1.0

New features

  • plot_fissure_vent(): state 1 vs state 2 deuteration plot with per-peptide Welch confidence ellipses (an ellipse touching the diagonal means the peptide’s own p-value is above the cutoff) and the pooled Hageman & Weis critical-interval band.
  • Interactive, linked views: interactive_volcano(), interactive_fissure_vent(), interactive_woods(), interactive_fissure_explorer() (plotly/crosstalk).
  • Multi-state comparisons: compare_states_tp() (three or more states, Welch ANOVA omnibus plus pairwise hybrid tests, optional BH correction; by = "sequence" or by = "position" peptide matching) and compare_states_unmatched() (region-level comparison when peptide maps differ between states, with a per-peptide diagnostic), with plot_compare_states_tp(), plot_compare_states_unmatched() and plot_coverage_diagnostics().
  • Per-residue analysis: residue_deconvolution(), residue_level_average(), residue_regions(), residue_regions_subset_summary().
  • Structure mapping: plot_hdx_structure(), plot_hdx_structure_legend().
  • Data quality: plot_peptide_coverage_map(); long-format helpers boxer_input_to_long() and all_data_long_input().
  • New vignettes: fissure vent, interactive explorer, multi-state (anova), structure mapping, data quality. The unfinished correlation-plots vignette was removed.

Interface and documentation

  • Argument names are consistent: pvalue (was pv_cutoff) and col (was cola / colors_initial). The old names still work, with a deprecation warning. As in 0.0.2, pv_cutoff sets both the p-value cutoff and the critical-interval alpha (unless alpha is given).
  • The plotting and PyMOL functions now have separate alpha and pvalue arguments, placed where pv_cutoff was. Calls that pass these values by position (e.g. plot_heat_map_tp(a, 3.5, ranges, 0.05, 3)) now set different arguments: name the arguments. CI_factor was removed from the robot and Woods plot functions; use alpha.
  • PyMOL script functions gain resno_offset to match structure numbering.
  • Internal helper functions are marked internal (still exported; hidden from the help index).
  • The _proc functions are documented as percent-deuteration counterparts of their uptake versions (significance on uptake, differences shown in percent deuteration).
  • New example data three_states.csv (wild type and two point mutants, uneven replicates; Woods et al. 2025, PNAS).
  • New vignette("input_formats"); README rewritten; pkgdown reference grouped by task; main vignette shows its summary/output code and points to the newer tools; stale references to removed functions fixed.

Reporting

  • New render_report(): one-command HTML report with the analysis parameters, the summary table, data-quality checks, significant-peptide counts and fissure-vent plots per time point, and optionally region ANOVAs and whole-time-course results; the tidy results table is written next to it.
  • New hdx_summary_table(): the summary table recommended by Masson et al.
      • computed items (time course, controls, replicates, peptides, coverage, length, redundancy, back-exchange, repeatability, significance threshold) plus your own experimental details via metadata; csv or markdown.
  • New hdx_results_table(): tidy per-peptide, per-time, per-pair results (means, SDs, n, difference, p-value, adjusted p-value, CI, call), written as csv with a _parameters.txt file holding the parameters and sessionInfo().
  • Results of compare_states_tp(), compare_states_unmatched(), compare_regions(), compare_timecourse(), residue_regions(), plot_fissure_vent() and the new tables carry their parameters, the package version and the date as attribute "hdxboxer".
  • compare_states_unmatched() gains seed for reproducible resampling.
  • output_prep(): Mean.Peptide_Mass_[Da] is now the measured neutral peptide mass (Charge x (centroid m/z - proton mass)); it previously held the centroid m/z. The percent column is labelled [%] instead of [Da], column names are no longer mangled (_[Da] instead of _.Da.), and the table is returned invisibly.
  • general_info()/all_summary(): average peptide length counts residues (End - Start + 1); it was one residue too short.

Statistics: one significance rule, regions and time courses

  • One significance rule everywhere: a peptide differs when its Welch p-value is below pvalue AND its difference exceeds the pooled critical interval. p-values are raw by default; every function that calls significance now takes p_adjust (e.g. "BH"), including pv_timepoint(), pv_timecourse(), the heat map, volcano, Woods, robot and peptide plots, the PyMOL scripts, plot_fissure_vent(), the interactive plots, diff_peptides_prep() and verbose_timepoint_output().
  • compare_states_tp(): raw p-values by default (p_adjust = "none"; previously BH) and a Welch one-way ANOVA as the reported omnibus test (omnibus = "kruskal" for the previous Kruskal-Wallis test). p_adjust_method is deprecated. A peptide in two overlapping regions now enters the multiple-testing correction once.
  • residue_regions(): peptides are called by the package-wide rule (previously BH-adjusted p < fdr_cutoff with no critical interval; fdr_cutoff still works, deprecated, and reproduces that rule). Charge states of one peptide count once towards min_peptides, and the per-residue effect is the difference per exchangeable amide.
  • compare_states_unmatched(): the per-peptide diagnostic uses the package-wide rule, is listed first in summary, and its per-peptide results are returned as peptides; the pooled test is documented as approximate. p_adjust replaces p_adjust_method (default now "none").
  • New compare_regions(): region-level two-way ANOVA (peptide + state) for matched peptides, with each peptide as its own control; pairwise state contrasts, a state x peptide heterogeneity test, and an optional model over all time points with a state x time test.
  • New compare_timecourse(): per-peptide summed difference over the time course with a global critical interval, and the number of time points at which a peptide is significant. robot_indexes(), robot_indexes_df() and robot_plot_All() gain min_timepoints.
  • New percent = "per_residue" in output_tp()/output_tc(): uptake per exchangeable amide, so peptide length does not affect the critical-interval half of the rule.
  • plot_fissure_vent() returns (invisibly) the table of what it drew.
  • The multi-state vignette is now vignette("multistate").

Fully deuterated control and quality checks

  • output_tp()/output_tc() gain percent = "FD": percent of the measured fully deuterated control, 100 * uptake / FD uptake of the same peptide and state (FD replicates averaged, charge states pooled), which corrects for back-exchange and D2O content. Peptides without a usable FD value (missing, or FD uptake <= 0) keep their row with empty (NA) values. percent = TRUE still returns the input’s own percent deuteration (HDXExaminer Deut %, relative to the theoretical maximum).
  • New peptide_qc() lists per peptide and state: missing undeuterated control, uptake reported as 0 at every time (a missing reference rather than a real measurement), negative uptake, FD uptake, theoretical maximum, FD fraction, and FD missing / <= 0 / above the maximum. It only reports; nothing is removed.
  • as_hdx_long() computes default percent deuteration against the same theoretical maximum as HDXExaminer and DynamX (length - 1 - prolines after the first residue).

Input formats

  • New read_hdx() reads HDXExaminer “All results” tables and Waters DynamX cluster and state exports (DynamX 2.x and 3.x), detecting the format from the header. read_hdxexaminer() and read_dynamx() read one format explicitly. For DynamX cluster data each raw file is a replicate and uptake is computed from the centroid mass; on a public matched cluster/state data set it agrees with DynamX’s own uptake (r = 0.9999). fd = marks the fully deuterated control (a control state, or each state’s last time point); combine_charges = TRUE merges charge states.
  • New as_hdx_long() builds HDXBoxeR input from a long table exported by any other software, with times in s, min or h.
  • Every function that takes filepath now also accepts a DynamX file or a table from read_hdx()/as_hdx_long(); reading once and passing the table avoids re-reading the file in every call.

Uneven and missing replicates

  • output_tp() and output_tc() now use every replicate of every state by default, so states may have different numbers of replicates (e.g. 3 and 4). Previously all states were cut to the smallest count and the extra replicates were silently dropped; replicates = n still caps the number.
  • A peptide with a missing measurement is kept with NA instead of being dropped, as long as it has at least min_replicates (new argument, default 2) values in every state. Dropped peptides are reported.
  • sd_timepoint(), ave_timepoint(), pv_timepoint(), sd_ci_timepoint() and pv_timecourse() find each state’s replicate columns by name and ignore missing values; pv_timepoint() returns NA instead of failing when a peptide has fewer than two values or identical replicates.
  • CI_2pts() (and so CI_tp(), CI_tc() and every plot using them) pools each state’s SDs weighted by their degrees of freedom and uses each state’s own number of replicates. With equal, complete replicates the result is unchanged.
  • The results of output_tp()/output_tc() record their replicates, states, times and units as attributes.
  • State names are matched exactly before abbreviations are tried, so a state “WT” is no longer confused with “WT_mut”.
  • output_tc(seq_match = ) now means the same as in output_tp() (FALSE: identical sequence required; TRUE: match by position). The two functions previously used opposite meanings. With seq_match = TRUE, output_tp() keeps its usual column order (Sequence fourth).
  • compare_states_tp() uses every replicate by default (replicates = NULL).

Changes to results

  • Robot plots, Woods plots, robot_indexes() and robot_indexes_df(): p-values and averages came from two tables sorted differently (by Start as text in one, as a number in the other) and were combined row by row, so the wrong peptides could be called significant. This was also the case in 0.0.2. Both tables now have the same order.

  • plots_vol_tp() colors each state with its own critical interval instead of the largest one.

  • plot_heat_map_tp_proc(): the default ranges is c(-Inf, seq(-30, 30, by = 10), Inf), as documented (it was ten times smaller).

  • backHX_calculations() averages the replicate centroids of each peptide before the calculation, so the range is over peptides; a state without FD or undeuterated data gives NA.

  • output_UD() and the time-course tables treat a missing undeuterated uptake (HDXExaminer n/a, DynamX) as 0, so average_timecourse(), sd_timecourse() and their _proc versions work with such data.

  • backHX_calculations() now computes back-exchange from the measured centroid times charge, (Exp Cent[FD] - Exp Cent[0s]) * Charge. It previously used the theoretical centroid m/z without the charge factor, which overstated back-exchange roughly in proportion to the charge state.

  • plot_fissure_vent() (default sd_source = "raw"), the interactive plots and residue_regions() now build the critical interval from each state’s raw replicate SD, so it matches CI_tp(), diff_peptides_prep() and the heat map, Woods and robot plots. sd_source = "CI" keeps the previous, wider band.

  • All critical-interval functions (CI_2pts(), CI_tp(), CI_tc(), CI_single(), compare_timecourse()) use the same two-tailed t-value, qt(alpha/2, df), as in HDXBoxeR 0.0.2 and Janowska et al. (2024).

  • Multiple-testing correction (p_adjust) uses one family everywhere: the peptides of one pair of states at one time point.

  • sd_ci_timepoint() uses the correct conversion from a two-sided interval to an SD (factor of 2 and alpha/2).

  • general_info() reports the real number of replicates.

Bug fixes

  • replicates is now honoured by woods_CI_plot(), woods_CI_plot_frac(), robot_plot_All(), robot_indexes(), robot_indexes_df(), pymol_script_significant_residue(), pymol_script_significant_residue_proc() and summary_sd_CI().
  • robot_indexes()/robot_indexes_df() keep significant peptides from every state, not only the last one.
  • compare_states_unmatched() treats each charge state as its own peptide instead of pooling charge states as extra replicates.
  • plot_cor_pts_elps(): ellipse position and axis fixed.
  • output_prep(): fully deuterated rows no longer report a fake SD of 100.
  • residue_deconvolution()/residue_level_average() use the same exchangeable-residue convention as nb_exch_deut().
  • all_data_long_input() no longer fails on an undefined variable; boxer_input_to_long() parses percent-deuteration columns correctly.
  • vol_tp() default palette size no longer reads stats::df.
  • Peptides are matched between states without the retention time, so a small RT shift no longer splits one peptide into two rows.
  • output_FD(), output_UD() and their _proc versions return every state (previously only the last one); output_UD() also finds an undeuterated control written as "0s".
  • robot_indexes_df() returns the peptide keys (Start, End, Sequence, Charge); robot_indexes() returns rows of the table used by the robot plots.
  • general_info() and all_summary(): coverage is computed over protein_range (new argument), and redundancy over covered residues. all_summary() works without back-exchange data.
  • summary_sd_CI() pools SDs correctly with uneven replicates.
  • The _proc functions stop when the uptake and percent tables are not aligned row by row.
  • PyMOL scripts take the state names from the column names correctly.
  • significant_peptide_uptake() no longer fails on missing values.
  • plot_fissure_vent() gains xlim/ylim; its returned table includes Charge.
  • read_dynamx(fd = "last") warns when states have different longest exposures.
  • read_dynamx(): a state without its own undeuterated run (e.g. an FD control) uses the undeuterated mass of the same peptide from the other states, with a message.
  • compare_states_tp() stops when given more than one time point.
  • residue_deconvolution() and residue_level_average() use the plain sequence and the Start-End range, so joined sequences (seq_match = TRUE) or DynamX modifications no longer spread uptake beyond the peptide; nb_exch_deut() ignores modifications.
  • PyMOL functions work with the default path = "" (working directory).
  • pymol_script_significant_residue_proc() keeps input_up first (as in 0.0.2) and swaps the two tables, with a warning, when they are given the other way round.
  • Interactive plots treat charge states of one peptide as separate peptides; vector alpha/pvalue no longer break interactive_woods() and significant_peptides_table().
  • output_prep() uses every replicate by default, handles uneven replicates and missing centroids.
  • plot_hdx_structure() matches state names exactly.
  • State names in plot legends and titles are no longer cut short for percent tables.
  • Average, difference and volcano plots work with NA values (e.g. percent = "FD" tables).
  • seq_match = TRUE with three or more states lists each sequence once; time labels in minutes or hours sort by time.
  • hdx_summary_table() gains states; the report summary uses the report’s states.

Documentation and packaging

  • Test suite added (testthat 3rd edition).
  • ?All_results_table documents the example input file.
  • URL and BugReports added to DESCRIPTION.
